transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I keep getting light-headed and dizzy when I stand up, like I'm about to faint. It started about ten days ago, and it's been happening several times a day since.
Could you describe how much this is affecting your everyday life, and whether you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?
I've stopped going to my Tuesday lunch club because I'm worried about feeling faint on the bus. As for allergies, I don't have any that I know of — no bad reactions to medicines.

Could you tell me about any medicines you take regularly or have taken recently—including anything new or changed, and the dose if you know it—and about any long-term health conditions, past illnesses, operations, or hospital stays you’ve had?

I take a water tablet, bendroflumethiazide 2.5 mg, every morning and have done for years. About two and a half weeks ago the practice nurse added a new blood-pressure tablet, amlodipine 5 mg once daily, for high readings. I also take a small tablet for my stomach each morning but I can't remember its name, and paracetamol 1 g up to three times a day for hip pain.

For long-term conditions, I've had high blood pressure for about 15 years and osteoarthritis in both hips. I can't recall any operations or hospital stays.
When the light-headedness comes on, how severe would you say it feels, for example on a scale from 0 to 10?
I'd rate it about 6 out of 10. I nearly fell once and had to grab the kitchen worktop, though I haven't actually fallen.
When you get that light-headed, dizzy feeling, what else do you notice at the same time, and are there any things that don’t happen?
It feels like a swimmy, about-to-faint feeling rather than the room spinning. I don't get chest pain, palpitations, blackouts, or any weakness in my arms or legs.
When that swimmy, about-to-faint feeling comes on, where do you feel it in your body, and does it spread anywhere?
I can't say it's in one particular spot — it's just a general swimmy feeling, mostly in my head, and it doesn't spread anywhere. It comes over me and then settles if I sit back down for a minute.
Just to make sure I have the full picture: apart from the tablets you’ve mentioned, do you take any other medicines for your blood pressure or your hips — or is that all?
No, that's all — just the bendroflumethiazide and the new amlodipine for my blood pressure, and the paracetamol for my hips. I don't take anything else for those.

Aside from your blood pressure and hip pain, is there anything else you see a doctor or nurse about regularly—such as the reason for your small stomach tablet—or any operations or hospital stays in the past?

The small tablet is just something for my stomach each morning, but I can't remember what it's called or much more about it. Other than my blood pressure and hips, I don't see anyone regularly, and I can't recall any operations or hospital stays.

To make sure I’ve got the full list, is there anything else you take at other times of day, anything that isn’t a tablet like an inhaler, eye drops, cream, injection or patch, or anything you buy without a prescription such as painkillers, vitamins or herbal remedies—or is it just what you’ve already told me?
No, there's nothing else — no inhalers, eye drops, creams, injections or patches, and I don't buy anything like vitamins or herbal remedies. It's just the tablets I've already told you about.
What worries you most about these light-headed, dizzy feelings when you stand up, and what are you hoping we can help with today?
I'm worried the new blood-pressure tablet is causing this, and I'd like to know whether I should stop taking it. That's the main thing I'm hoping you can help me with today.

Since these light-headed, dizzy feelings started, have you noticed any changes in your appetite, sleep, weight or energy, or any changes in your bladder, bowels or breathing—or has none of that changed?
No, I haven't noticed any changes in my appetite, sleep, weight or energy, and nothing different with my bladder, bowels or breathing either.
Is there anything else that came along with these dizzy, light-headed feelings that we haven’t talked about yet?
No, nothing else has come along with them — just the swimmy, about-to-faint feeling and nothing more.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
